text:
The plate holds a single small piece of corn on the cob, a cross-section about 3 cm thick and 5 cm across, plus a couple of stray kernels. It looks like a cob segment with the kernels mostly eaten or sitting on it.

Estimated mass is about 60 g for the cob piece with its kernels, plus a few grams of loose kernels, so roughly 65 g in total.

Corn kernels run about 90 kcal per 100 g. The cob itself adds little, so I assumed about 0.9 kcal/g on the edible part, or roughly 55 kcal for 65 g. Part of that mass is the cob core, which isn't eaten, so I lowered the figure to about 50 kcal.

{"kcal": 50, "mass_g": 65}
